messages:
Emma: Quick heads-up — I opened a PR that stitches together the Optimize playbook, SDK examples (py/go/js) and a short migration checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
Noah: Linking it here. Can you call out the KV-prefetch caveat for short-seq workloads? We've seen p95 regressions when prefetch is enabled without tuning.
Emma: Good call. Added a new section "Short-sequence prefetch" and an example. snippet:
```yaml
quant_profiles:
  short_seq:
    dtype: q4_0
    kv_prefetch: true
```
Liam: The YAML looks fine, but `q4_0` needs a note about token alignment and warmed KV cache. Put: "recommended only for <=128 tokens and with warm cache". Also mention impact on cold-start latency.
Emma: Done — I added the sentence and a short table showing tradeoffs. Also added a small Go SDK example for batching + prefetch, could someone sanity-check it? Link in the PR.
Sophie: I'll review. Also can we recommend a canary rollout pattern in the migration steps? Ops asked for a concrete policy (percent steps + monitors). Suggestion: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring on token_cost and latency_p95.
Emma: Added a sample rollout JSON: 
```json
{"rollout": "5%->25%->100%", "monitor": ["latency_p95","token_cost"]}
```
Noah: small ask — call out the console traces link and the query to detect token alignment regressions. Put a note: `SELECT pct FROM evals WHERE sample_type='short_seq'` (pseudo).
docs-bot: @Emma Reminder created: JIRA-OPT-381 (docs: add redirect and rollout example) :bell:
Maria: quick nit — the Go snippet uses `Batcher` which was renamed to `BatcherV2` in SDK v0.9.2.
Emma: Thanks, fixed the snippet and added a compatibility note for SDK versions <0.9.2.
Liam: I'll take a pass on the quant guidance tomorrow morning; I'll pay special attention to the wording around fallback to fp16 for safety.
Sophie: After Liam's sign-off I'll do a language pass and checklist (links, anchors, redirects). Aiming to merge by EOD Thursday.
Emma: One more thing — can someone confirm the example link for the Python prefetch helper? I added https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/prefetch-helpers but it may be private.
Noah: That repo is internal; for public docs we need a sanitized snippet. Maybe copy the minimal helper into the docs examples dir.
Emma: Will extract a minimal snippet and add a short HOWTO.
Sophie: Tiny UX note — put the migration checklist as collapsible steps in the page so readers can expand each verification step.
Emma: Good idea, done.
Liam: Quick technical comment: recommend we add an explicit sentence: "If using quantized short-seq profiles, test with a representative prompt set (>=2000 samples) and measure p95/p99 latency and exact-match delta."
Emma: Added that testing guidance and a small script in examples to generate the representative prompt set.
Noah: Please add a one-liner to the release notes summarizing: "Docs: Optimize toolkit — KV-prefetch and short-sequence quant profiles guidance + migration playbook".
Emma: Added to release notes draft. Thanks everyone :party_parrot: 
Sophie: LGTM pending Liam's tech sign-off.
Liam: I'll post comments in the PR by 09:30 PDT tomorrow.
Emma: Awesome — TY all, will keep the PR open for the review cycle.
